relevance_note: The paper describes named patients with HA20 ("16 patients with HA20") and gives individual-level data (sex, age, severity, stomatitis, abdominal symptoms, medication) for 16 patients and 15 of their relatives in Supplementary Table 1, but prints no TNFAIP3 variant for anyone.
method_note: Table transcription: Supplementary Table 1 (16 patients, 15 relatives) and the text were read directly; every value and span was transcribed cell by cell from the Markdown table and each span was checked to occur verbatim in the paper (grep). No TNFAIP3 variant is printed anywhere in the paper for any patient, so each of the 16 patients gets a variants row with variant_original_string 'not reported' (v3, D-22); no variant rows are made for the 15 relatives, whose variant status is nowhere stated. Labels: the paper's own IDs P3-P22 (Supplementary Table 1: 'The current ID of the patients is the same as the ID at the previous report (1).') and the relative IDs '<patient>-fa/-mo/-sib' ('P, patient; fa, Father; mo, mother; sib, sibling'). One relative, P8/P9-mo, is the mother of two patients and has one label. Relatives are in scope as relatives of patients ('Characteristics and microbiome diversity of the patients with HA20 and their relatives'); the paper calls them 'healthy family members' / 'healthy relatives'. Scope decisions: the study enrolled 18 patients, but only 16 (patients 3-5, 7-13, 17-22) appear in Supplementary Table 1; the remaining patients are mentioned only as counts and are not identifiable ('Clinical characteristics of the patients were previously reported (patients 3–5, 7–13, and 17–22)'), so they get no rows. The person called 'a sibling whose genetic information is unknown' and the healthy family members not listed in Supplementary Table 1 are mentioned only as counts/without any individual-level detail, so they get no rows either; they are counted in cohort_size_as_stated. is_proband is false for everyone (the paper calls no one a proband); no span is possible for a negative, so the span is null. Contradictions: the Results say 'Thirty-one fecal samples from 16 patients and 15 healthy family members were sequenced' while the abstract says 'Stool samples were obtained from 16 patients with HA20 and 15 of their family members'; the sample numbers analysed differ (13 vs 13) because samples were excluded. Checklist mapping: the item 'oral ulcers' is recorded from the Supplementary Table 1 column 'Stomatitis' (yes/no), the only oral finding; the paper never uses the word 'ulcer'. 'Abdominal symptoms' is recorded as a phenotypic feature only, never as 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation', because the paper says 'not all patients with HA20 received gastrointestinal endoscopy, and so alternative indicators such as the disease severity or abdominal symptoms do not necessarily reflect the exact intestinal condition'. The column 'Antibiotics use from 6 months to 4 weeks ago' records antibiotic exposure, not infections, so it is not used for 'recurrent infections'. 'Nobody but an excluded younger brother (P22-sib) has food allergies' is treated as individual-level for P22-sib only, not as excluding food allergy for everyone else, because it does not name the group explicitly and its scope (participants vs analysed samples) is unclear. The '-' cells in the relatives' rows of Supplementary Table 1 (Severity, Stomatitis, Abdominal symptoms) are not defined as negative by the legend, so they are 'not reported' (v3, D-22); the legend defines only '*' (younger than 3 years) and the dagger (antibiotics within 4 weeks). Counts without names ('Eleven of 13 patients and eight of 13 presented with stomatitis and abdominal symptoms', 'four and five patients' with/without autoantibodies, 'Patients with HA20 consist of four mild, four moderate, and five severe patients') are never used to exclude a feature. Ages in Supplementary Table 1 are ages at stool-sample collection ('sex, age at the sample collection') and are recorded as age_at_last_evaluation; no age at onset or at diagnosis is given for anyone. disease_label_as_stated is left 'not reported' for the relatives, described only as 'healthy family members'; clinical_diagnosis_basis is 'not reported' for everyone (the diagnosis is not described). The separator ' / ' does not occur in any table of this paper, so D-31 raised no issue; the two stacked header blocks of Supplementary Table 2 (phylum counts) are used only to order the patients ('The healthy family members (upper) and patients (lower) are represented in order of age'). The Discussion sentence about 'one refractory patient successfully received hematopoietic cell transplantation (Shiraki et al., 2021)' concerns a previously published person with no individual-level fact, so no row was created. source_reference_in_review is 'not reported' for every person: Supplementary Table 1 has no per-patient source column, and the table footnote ('The current ID of the patients is the same as the ID at the previous report (1).') applies to the whole table; these patients are described first-hand in this study, and the earlier report is recorded in publications.prior_report_citation. Variants rows: the paper never prints a TNFAIP3 variant for any person and never says which patients were tested, but it labels all 16 as patients with HA20, the disease it defines as 'Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20)' caused by the TNFAIP3 gene, so each of the 16 gets one variants row with variant_original_string 'not reported'; gene_symbol_as_stated 'TNFAIP3' is quoted from the paper's gene description and not from a per-patient statement; all other variant fields are 'not reported' because no individual-level variant statement exists.
